avoid.reason: Watch drinks and bar bills in Itaewon and Hongdae nightlife late at night, and mind belongings in Myeongdong's shopping crowds.

hood_desc: A bustling downtown shopping and street-food district packed with cosmetics stores, fashion outlets and crowds. Ideal for shoppers and first-time visitors who want central convenience.
A youthful, energetic neighborhood around Hongik University known for indie music, street art, clubs and cheap eats. Best for students and night owls seeking a creative, budget-friendly scene.
An affluent, glossy district of luxury boutiques, upscale dining, plastic-surgery clinics and stylish nightlife. Suits visitors wanting modern, high-end and trend-conscious Seoul.
A traditional cultural quarter with antique shops, tea houses, art galleries and craft studios. Perfect for those seeking Korean heritage, souvenirs and a slower pace.
A diverse, international district near the former US base with global restaurants, bars and a multicultural crowd. Great for travelers wanting varied cuisine and an eclectic nightlife.

water.note: Tap water meets safety standards, though many locals still prefer boiled or filtered water for taste.

transit.pay: Buy a T-money card at any convenience store (GS25, CU, 7-Eleven) or station machine for ~3,000–5,000 won (~US$2–4) and top up with cash — it covers subway, buses and even taxis, with a base subway fare of about 1,550 won (~US$1.10). Foreign contactless bank cards can't be tapped at the gates yet (rollout runs through 2030), so the card is essential.
transit.hours: The subway runs about 5:30am to midnight; late-night 'Owl' (N) buses cover major routes overnight.

landmarks: Gyeongbokgung Palace
The grandest of Seoul's Joseon-era royal palaces, with sweeping courtyards and mountain backdrop that make it endlessly photogenic, especially with visitors in rented hanbok.
N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower)
Perched atop Namsan Mountain, it offers the definitive 360-degree panoramic photo of Seoul's skyline, especially at sunset.
Bukchon Hanok Village
A hillside neighborhood of centuries-old traditional hanok houses with narrow alleys, prized for picturesque, timeless streetscape shots.
Lotte World Tower
South Korea's tallest skyscraper, its sleek glass spire dominates the Seoul skyline and observation deck views.
Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)
Zaha Hadid's futuristic, curving neofuturistic building lit up at night is one of Seoul's most striking modern architectural landmarks.
Changdeokgung Palace
A UNESCO World Heritage palace famed for its Secret Garden (Huwon), offering elegant traditional architecture amid natural landscaping.
Myeongdong
Seoul's buzzing shopping and street-food district, anchored by the Gothic-spired Myeongdong Cathedral, vibrant with neon signage at night.
Han River Parks
The river that bisects Seoul, flanked by parks and bridges (like Banpo Bridge's Rainbow Fountain), popular for skyline and sunset photography.
Insadong
A historic cultural district of traditional teahouses, galleries, and craft shops, beloved for atmospheric alley photos.
Namdaemun Market / Namdaemun Gate
Seoul's oldest surviving city gate stands beside its largest traditional market, blending centuries-old heritage with everyday street life.

train.note: No international trains run from South Korea - the border with North Korea is closed, so the country is effectively an island for rail. Domestically, KTX high-speed trains fan out from Seoul Station to Busan, Gwangju and beyond; the separate SRT high-speed service (etk.srail.kr) uses Suseong Station in the south of the city.

bus.note: There are no international coach routes - South Korea has no open land border. Long-distance express buses (gosok) run nationwide from Seoul Express Bus Terminal and Central City Terminal; book through the integrated operator site Kobus (kobus.co.kr).

ferry.note: International ferries to China leave from the Incheon International Passenger Terminal, about an hour west of central Seoul (not from Seoul itself) - bring your passport. Weidong Ferry sails overnight to Weihai and Qingdao; other operators serve Dandong, Tianjin and more. Ferries to Japan (Busan-Fukuoka etc.) depart from Busan, not the Seoul area.
